headline: USD is stronger than it's been in weeks, with $1 now buying about 0.88 EUR.
summary: Both the Fed and ECB raised interest rates this month for the first time in years, largely because an oil-price shock tied to Middle East tensions pushed inflation back up in both regions. Markets had already priced in these hikes, so the bigger driver of recent moves has been Fed officials signaling more hikes may follow, while the ECB has sounded less certain about doing the same. That shifting expectation gap — not any single headline — has pushed the dollar broadly higher over the past couple of weeks.
forYou: If you're moving USD into EUR right now, your dollars go a bit further than they did a month ago, though these rate-expectation shifts can move things around quickly in either direction.
